 Dated this the 22nd day of February, 2016  ORDER

The first accused in C.C.No.736 of 2002 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Vaikom, filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16 (1) (a) (ii) and 7 (v) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Vaikom
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.
The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 22.05.2002 at about 5.00 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 750 gram of peas dhal from the shop of the first accused.
After sampling as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis.

The Public Analyst, after analysis submitted Ext.P12 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food grain under the PFA Rules, 1955 and was therefore adulterated.
It was also alleged that the first accused sold the food item without having a valid licence under the PFA Rules.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts.P1 to P15 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 to DW3 were examined and Exts.D1 to D9 series were marked for the revision petitioner.

5. The trial court after appreciating the evidence, found the revision petitioner guilty under Sections 16 (1) (a)
(ii) and 7 (v) of the Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act r/w Rule 50 of the Prevention of the Food Adulteration Rules and convicted and sentenced him thereunder.

entities.text: Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Prevention of the Food Adulteration Rules
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the appeal, the conviction was confirmed and the sentence was modified.
The incident in this case was on 22.05.2002.
There is no previous conviction against the revision petitioner.
There is also no allegation that the revision petitioner was involved in any other offence of similar nature, after the incident in this case.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the appellate court had sentenced the revision petitioner under second proviso to Section 16 (1) of the PFA Act.
The courts below correctly appreciated the evidence and concurrently found that the revision petitioner did not have a valid licence to sell the food item under the PFA Rules.

There is absolutely nothing on record to indicate K.D.Sundaran vs Food Inspector on 22 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53474079/
2 that the revision petitioner had a valid licence under the PFA Rules during the relevant period.

entities.text: K.D.Sundaran vs Food Inspector on 22 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that the revision petitioner applied for the renewal of the licence subsequent to the incident in this case.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the sentence awarded by the appellate court can be modified and reduced to imprisonment till the rising of the court and a fine of Rs.500/- (Rupees five hundred only) and in default to simple imprisonment for five days under Sections 16 (1) (a) (ii) and 7 (v) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, to meet the ends of justice and accordingly I order so.
In the result, this revision petition stands allowed in part as above.
The revision petitioner shall surrender before the court below on 5.4.2016 to suffer the sentence.

Sd/-
B. SUDHEENDRA KUMAR JUDGE Scl/23.02.2016
